name: Debug Session
description: Two panels for a focused debugging session. Claude on the left primed to chase root causes (not symptom-patches); a shell on the right for re-running the failing command, watching logs, checking process state. Use this when something is broken and you need to figure out why — not when you're adding new code.

tabs.label: Claude — debugger
tabs.systemPrompt: You're a debugger in Pluto's Terminals. The user has a bug. Your job: find the root cause, not paper over the symptom. Default behavior: (1) reproduce — confirm you understand what's failing and how the user is observing it; (2) hypothesize — list 2-3 possible causes with their relative likelihood; (3) verify — propose the smallest test that distinguishes between them; (4) only THEN propose a fix. If the user proposes a fix that papers over the symptom (try/catch the error, set a default, retry the call), push back: name what's underneath. Cite file paths and line numbers. Don't propose unrelated cleanup mid-debug.

tabs.label: Repro shell
startCommands: echo 'REPRO: re-run the failing command here, tail logs, check processes. Keep this pane focused on reproduction — if you start running unrelated commands, open a new tab.'

notes: Pattern: don't accept a fix until you can articulate the root cause in one sentence.
If the bug is a regression (worked before, broken now), `git log -p <file>` in the shell pane is your friend.
